chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal from Yunus ibn Yaqub who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Nothing that comes to us from your area is more beloved to me than rice and the violet. I complained of that severe pain, so I was inspired to eat rice. So I ordered it to be washed and dried, then fried and ground, and made for me as an oiled powder and a cooked dish which I would consume, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed that pain from me.'

key_terms.الْبَنَفْسَجِ: Violet (or a type of fragrant plant/flower)
key_terms.سَفُوفٌ: A dry, powdered food mixture, often medicinal

ai.seo_question: What is the medicinal benefit of rice according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the medicinal value of rice, noting it as his preferred sustenance from Kufa, particularly for alleviating severe pain. He describes a specific preparation method—washing, drying, frying, grinding, and cooking with oil—to create a therapeutic dish that cured his ailment, reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating practical health remedies with spiritual inspiration (ilhām). This narration underscores the importance of dietary medicine in Islamic tradition, linking physical well-being to divine guidance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, and Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There has not been brought to us<sup>asws</sup> from your areas anything more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup> than the rice, and the viola. I<sup>asws</sup> complained of intense pain, so I<sup>asws</sup> was inspired to eat the rice. So I<sup>asws</sup> ordered with it, so it was washed and dried. Then it was fried, and ground, so it was made from me<sup>asws</sup> as an oiled powder, and cooked, so I<sup>asws</sup> took it, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made that pain to go away from me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from and al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’From your area no other thing comes more desirable to me than rice and viola. I had intense pain and I was inspired to eat rice. I ordered to wash it, dry it, and pick up to grind it, then in a powder form with oil and a mixture, I drank it. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, removed with it that pain.”’
